dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle fired at about 20:30 ET on 2026-09-24, the evening of S itself, rather than at 10:30 ET the following morning. That makes the blindness rule easier, not harder, because no session after S has opened; every figure here is dated at or before the 2026-09-24 close. Costco and Darden reported after the 16:00 bell on S and are therefore excluded from the vote facts even though they carry the date 2026-09-24.

Spot gold: Investing.com's XAU/USD table now shows a 2026-09-23 close of 4288.68, where the 2026-09-23 document recorded 4287.35 from the same feed's previous-close field. The 2026-09-23 horizon was scored on the STORED basis of 4287.35 against a 2026-09-24 close of 4286.06; the outcome is flat under either base. Vendor dispersion on S remains wide: TheStreet quotes 4293 (-0.56%), Investrade 4298.00 (-0.47%) and Kitco 4283.40 late-session. 4286.06 is recorded to keep the whole series on one vendor.

The 2026-09-24 30-year yield is the run's worst vendor conflict. Investing.com shows 5.409 (+0.7bp), which cannot be reconciled with TLT's actual -1.29% close; Investrade gives 5.446 and the news log 5.476, both of which reconcile via the -0.165 %/bp rule. Because a clean TLT price history was obtainable from stockanalysis.com this run, the driver regression uses actual TLT closes and the 30-year proxy the 2026-09-23 document had to rely on is retired. The Investing.com 30-year print for S is flagged unreliable.

The 2026-09-24 2-year is 4.941 on Investing.com against 4.918 from TheStreet and the news log and 4.89 from Saxo. Investing.com is used throughout so the regression series is internally consistent; the 2.3bp spread does not change any vote sign or any dominant-driver classification.

TLT 30-day implied volatility of 13.39 is carried unchanged from the 2026-09-23 document, where it was itself derived rather than sourced. No 2026-09-24 30-day ATM print exists on any source reached; HPSILab's 12.88% references the 7 October expiry, a different construction. One session stale, well inside the two-week window. The bond stretch components are insensitive to the choice: extension50 scores -2 for any sigma between about 11.2 and 15.5.

GVZ 22.77 is YCharts' confirmed 2026-09-23 close. A Google Finance print of 22.58 stamped 16:02 ET on 2026-09-24 was rejected because GVZ disseminates until 16:15 ET, so it is not a confirmed close. FRED GVZCLS lags to 23.59 on 2026-09-22. Gold was essentially unchanged on S, so the one-day-stale reading is close to right.

RVX 19.97 is YCharts' 2026-09-23 close; no 2026-09-24 print was obtainable and FRED RVXCLS lags to 2026-09-22. VXN 21.24 is moomoo's explicitly labelled 2026-09-24 close. Both are inside the two-week window. Because RVX is one day stale and rose 6.3% on 2026-09-23, the IWM bands here are probably slightly narrow.

EUR/USD 1-month implied volatility of 4.72 is carried from 2026-09-21; three sessions stale, inside the two-week window, and used as the dollar sigma. No CVIX or dated EUR/USD implied-volatility print was obtainable from any source reached.

The dollar oscillator component is the run's most consequential soft number. DealPlexus gives DXY RSI(14) 70.8 in a snapshot stamped 05:48 ET on 2026-09-24, i.e. reflecting the 2026-09-23 close, and its SMA50 and SMA200 reproduce the prior document's 99.94 and 99.18 exactly, which validates the page. FXStreet independently gives 72.34 but its price includes 2026-09-25 Asian trading. DXY was flat on S at -0.01%, so the S-dated RSI is close to 70.8, but it sits near the 70 threshold: a value of 69.9 would score oscillator 0, dropping the dollar stretch score from +3 to +2 and turning the h1 and h5 overlay actions from an extreme-ride dampening into a stretched-ride dampening. The call and confidence outcome is identical either way (one notch down in both cases), so the sensitivity does not change the board.

No SPX, TLT, gold, IWM or QQQ RSI or moving average computed through the 2026-09-24 close survived cross-checking; Financhill and TipRanks values through the 2026-09-23 close are used, with the date recorded. These are one session stale, not live-session contaminated, so they are recorded rather than nulled. Investing.com's technical pages were rejected again: the SPX page collapses MA50 and MA200 onto each other at 7681, the SPY page prints a 200-day above spot, and the gold page's MA200 of 4321 is 229 points away from the twice-confirmed 4550.

The SPX 100-day moving average remains unobtainable; Financhill publishes no 100-day field and Investing.com's is corrupt. Recorded null. No category or overlay component depends on it.

driverRegime.notes: Re-measured this run. Gold's link to the 2-year is essentially unchanged from the 2026-09-24 baseline (corr -0.594 versus -0.59, beta -0.164 versus -0.176). The gold-TLT correlation has decayed to +0.374, just BELOW the +0.40 coherence threshold, from +0.41 a session earlier, so the pair no longer qualifies as a shared-driver pair on the full window; on big 2-year days it is still +0.463 with 5 of 7 sessions in the same direction. The cross-asset coherence check was therefore run but not triggered. TLT's own driver has shifted from the front end to the long end this week (corr to the 10-year -0.828 against -0.623 to the 2-year), consistent with 30-year yields setting a 22-year high. This run uses actual TLT closes rather than the -0.165 x 30-year-yield proxy the 2026-09-23 document had to use, because a clean TLT history was obtainable from stockanalysis.com.
